name: Distribución de Palabras Funcionales
description: Analyzes the distribution of function words (articles, prepositions, conjunctions) as stylistic fingerprints to distinguish AI from human text.
useCase: Detecting AI text through abnormal function word usage patterns that reflect unconscious writing style
mechanism: Extracts and quantifies function words (determiners, prepositions, conjunctions, auxiliary verbs, pronouns) which constitute ~50% of typical English text. These 'style words' are produced largely unconsciously by humans and carry strong authorial fingerprints. The method computes relative frequencies of 300+ function words and compares distributions using Burrows's Delta distance metric. AI-generated text shows statistically distinct function word profiles from human text.
source: Burrows, J. F. (2002) - Delta: A Measure of Stylistic Difference, Literary and Linguistic Computing
algorithm: Function Word Extraction + Burrows's Delta + Kilgarriff's Chi-Squared
parameters: Function word list: 300+ closed-class words, Metric: Burrows's Delta, z-score normalization, Granularity: per-paragraph, Reference: balanced human corpus
strengths:
• Grounded in decades of computational stylistics research
• Function words are difficult to consciously control
• Robust across topics and domains
• Well-understood statistical framework
limitations:
• Requires sufficient text length (>200 words)
• May not distinguish between different human authors vs AI
• Language-specific function word lists needed
• Modern LLMs increasingly match human distributions

references.title: Burrows, J. F. (2002). Delta: A Measure of Stylistic Difference and Its Literary History. Literary and Linguistic Computing.
Uchendu, A. et al. (2020). Authorship Attribution for Neural Text Generation. EMNLP.
Kestemont, M. (2014). Function Words in Authorship Attribution: From Black Magic to Theory? EACL Workshop.
